item.title: Describing the Fluxional Dynamics of Sub-nanoscale Clusters with Markov State Modeling
item.description:
Fluxionality, or the population of and interconversion between multiple structures, has long been suggested to be relevant for understanding the physical and catalytic behavior of sub-nanoscale metal clusters on an oxide support. Much of this treatment has, however, been thermodynamic, neglecting direct exploration of the timescales for interconversion between di!erent isomers. Previously, we exploited machine-learned interatomic potentials, combined with automatic process exploration (MLIP-APE) to identify isomerization networks for MgO-supported Pd clusters, capturing all barriers for cluster restructuring. In the current work, we demonstrate a new analysis approach based on Markov State Modeling (MSM) which captures the complex contribution of multiple timescales on the overall fluxional dynamic behavior over a range of cluster sizes. This overall fluxional behavior can then be classified between the extremes of highly dynamic “labile” clusters, to “rigid” clusters which exhibit much less dynamic behavior. These dynamics are of particular interest when using fluxional clusters for catalysis, as these dynamics could influence the observed catalytic reactions. Ultimately, this work demonstrates a rigorous and general approach to investigate the dynamics of reaction networks of well-defined states.

Patricia Poths, Feliks Nüske, Sebastian Matera, Karsten Reuter

item.title: The curious case of COF-300: One framework, Seventeen years of structural reinterpretation
item.description:
Few frameworks have changed the meaning of their own structural description as profoundly as COF-300. Over seventeen years, this archetypal three-dimensional covalent organic framework has evolved from a powder-derived interpenetrated model into a condition-dependent structural landscape. Successive studies revealed that conserved covalent connectivity can accommodate different interpenetration states, pronounced geometrical distortion, guest-selected conformers and large-amplitude breathing through coupled linker rotation, node deformation and interframework displacement. The structural problem subsequently expanded beyond the unit cell: crystal size, facets, local disorder, surfaces and composition alter mechanical response, while amorphous polymers, ordered molecular intermediates, classical growth and oriented attachment expose multiple routes by which crystallinity emerges. Recent advances go further, enabling crystallization trajectories, defects and even covalent linkages to be deliberately manipulated without necessarily erasing crystallographic identity. COF-300 is therefore better understood not through a single CIF, but as a history- and environment-dependent ensemble of states connected by kinetic pathways and energetic barriers. Its seventeen-year evolution reframes a broader challenge for dynamic reticular materials: structural determination must progress toward structural cartography, and reticular design from programming connectivity toward programming landscapes—the accessible states, transitions and histories through which a crystal acquires its behaviour.

Tsukasa Irie, Saikat Das, Yuichi Negishi

item.title: Central Atom Driven Modulation of Electron Transfer in Alkyne-Protected Ag <sub>14</sub> Nanoclusters
item.description:
Single-atom doping at the cluster core is an effective strategy for modulating the molecule-like properties of monolayer-protected nanoclusters. In this study, we systematically synthesized a pair of alkyne-protected silver nanoclusters, in which the central template anion of one nanocluster was replaced by a copper atom in the other. Incorporation of copper significantly quenched the photoluminescence of the nanocluster while enhancing its electron-transfer capability through modification of the electronic structure. Theoretical calculations further revealed that the central copper atom contributes directly to the frontier molecular orbitals. This work represents an important step toward the development of atomically precise nanochemistry, demonstrating how precise structural tailoring of alkyne-protected silver nanoclusters can be used to regulate their functional properties.

Rakendu Vinod, Meghna Ghosh, Xiaolin Liu, Rajannya Adhikary, Glory James, Nida Nahan Eyyakkandy, Subhrajyoti Bhandary, Pradip Kumar Mondal, Seiji Yamazoe, Soichi Kikkawa, De-en Jiang, Sukhendu Mandal
